source.passage: This section shall provide information for metadata fields that are common across the datasets. (Refer to CPD FFS 2.2.2 and SPD FFS 2.2.1) 2.2.1 Contractor. Provide the reporting contractor’s name, division (if applicable), facility location, mailing address, and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) or Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) code. 2.2.2 Contract. Provide the contract name (e.g., Low Rate Initial Production (LRIP) Lots 1-4), contract number, contract type, and applicable effort name (e.g., LRIP 1, Contract Line Item Number 1, Task 1). Effort name shall refer to the subdivision of reporting below the contract level. 2.2.3 Program. Provide the program name, or enter the type, model, and series or other military designation of the prime item or items purchased on the contract. The program phase (e.g., development, production) shall also be provided. 2.2.4 Report Period. Identify the current period covered by the reported data.

source.passage: A primary key constraint defines a collection of fields for a table such that the corresponding field values uniquely identify each record. No two records may have the same collection of corresponding field values.

condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: A foreign key constraint defines a correspondence between a field in one table and a field in another table such that the field value for each record in the former must match the field value for some record in the latter.

wording: The CPD shall resolve each non-null foreign-key field value to a corresponding record in the referenced table.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: Read with nullable-field rules in §2.1.2 and the table-specific nullability: valid null roots and inactive conditional foreign-key fields are permitted. String key comparisons are case-insensitive under §2.1.6.

source.passage: The following control characters are prohibited in all string values: (U+0000–U+0008), (U+000B– U+000C), (U+000E–U+001F), (U+007F). String values used as ID’s are further limited to a character set representing common printable characters (U+0020–U+007E).

wording: The CPD shall exclude U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, U+000E–U+001F and U+007F from string values and limit identifier strings to U+0020–U+007E.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: Most string values must have normalized whitespace. A string value with normalized whitespace cannot begin or end with whitespace characters, cannot contain any whitespace characters other than the space character (U+0020), and cannot contain any sequence of two or more contiguous space characters. Normalized whitespace is not required for string values used for remarks or other expository text.

wording: The CPD shall normalize String and StringID whitespace to single U+0020 spaces between text with no leading or trailing whitespace, except for remarks and other expository Text values.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: Empty string values are interpreted as equivalent to null values for fields with a string data type. Records must include non-empty string values for string fields that cannot be null.

wording: The CPD shall provide non-empty string values for string fields that cannot be null.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: The hierarchical structure of the WBS and OBS is determined based on the level and sequence of the elements reported. Specifically, elements must be sorted in a manner consistent with a depth-first search of the element hierarchy, such that the parent element of a given element must be the nearest preceding element with a reported level less than that of the given element. Each element that succeeds another must have a level that is no more than 1 greater than the level of the preceding element. The minimum level is 1.

wording: The CPD shall order WBS and OBS elements in depth-first hierarchy order, with each parent the nearest preceding lower-level element, a minimum level of one and a level increase no greater than one between consecutive elements.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: The first record must have Level equal to 1. All other records must have Level greater than 1. The first record must have a null ParentID. All other records must have a ParentID equal to the ID of the parent record determined by the hierarchical structure.

wording: Each CPD WBS or OBS table shall start with one Level 1 record having null ParentID and assign every subsequent record a Level greater than one and the ParentID of the parent determined by hierarchy order.
actor: Each CPD WBS or OBS table
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: The exact same source constraint appears in both WBS and OBS tables on PDF p11; retained as one shared obligation rather than duplicated by structure type.

source.passage: WBSElementID and OBSElementID must each refer to an element with no child elements (i.e. a terminal or leaf node in the respective hierarchical structure).

wording: The CPD shall map each control-account WBSElementID and OBSElementID to terminal elements in the respective WBS and OBS hierarchies.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: F10 scope: source responsibilities, organizational mapping or staffing data; not a claim to reproduce or accept the entire IPMDAR. Binding only under the recorded contract invocation and tailoring.

source.passage: Order of records is significant. Records must have contiguous, sequential ID values starting at 1 (i.e. 1, 2, 3, etc.). StartDate must be 1 day later than EndDate of the previous record, if any, and on or before EndDate of the current record. WorkHours must be greater than or equal to 0.

wording: The CPD reporting calendar shall use contiguous sequential IDs starting at one, contiguous non-overlapping inclusive date ranges and nonnegative working hours.
condition: When a native IPMDAR CPD Version 1.0 is supplied as operative staffing evidence under the recorded contract invocation
notes: Source use constraint says WorkHours whereas the table field is WorkingHours; retained verbatim and interpreted as the displayed WorkingHours field. IDs, date adjacency, date order and hours bounds are one calendar-validity obligation.

If EST_ToComplete_ByWorkPackage has a value of true, WorkPackageID must not be null and ControlAccountID must be null; otherwise, ControlAccountID must not be null and WorkPackageID must be null.

wording: The CPD BCWS_ToComplete and EST_ToComplete tables shall populate only WorkPackageID when the corresponding table-specific ByWorkPackage flag is true and only ControlAccountID when the flag is false.
actor: The CPD BCWS_ToComplete and EST_ToComplete tables

actor: The CPD BCWS_ToComplete and EST_ToComplete tables

source.passage: The name of each pair must exactly match the name of the corresponding field, and the value of each pair must follow the conventions below for representing the corresponding primitive data type in JSON. source.passage: Objects must include name/value pairs for fields that are not null, and these pairs must not have a JSON value of null or an empty JSON string value. Conversely, objects may or may not include name/value pairs for fields that are null. If included, these pairs must have a JSON value of null or an empty JSON string value. Only pairs for fields with a primitive data type of String, StringID, or Text may have an empty JSON string value.

wording: The CPD JSON records shall include non-null fields with non-null and non-empty values and represent included null fields as null or, for String, StringID and Text only, an empty string.

source.passage: Order of reporting periods is significant. Date ranges for sequential reporting periods must be exclusive and contiguous.
